answer: Aging a vault of earned reputation turns cheap identity creation into a slow, costly climb: each new agent starts with a locked, non-transferable bond in a shared vault, and only time plus verified useful work unlocks higher trust tiers. A sybil swarm can copy a relic of past success, but it cannot fake the months of attestations behind it. One bad act slashes the bond and sends a ripple through the agent's vouch graph, burning every sponsor who endorsed it, so creating many fake identities costs more than any single fraud can repay.
